items.name: inference-optimisation-skill
items.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
items.readme:
# inference-optimisation An agent skill for **hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server** on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: - single-user and concurrent decode - speculative decoding - prefill - KV cache size - startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: 1. Compute the theoretical ceiling. 2. Change one thing at a time. 3. Measure against interleaved controls. 4. Log every result, including the failures. 5. Gate on long-context retrieval. 6. Qualify a clean, pinned build before publishing. It works with Claude Code and any agent that loads `SKILL.md`-style skills. Any model can also follow it from [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). ## What we've been able to accomplish Results from the hill-climbs this skill was distilled from. Every number was measured on the hardware named; see the linked sources for methods and raw data. | Hardware | Model / quant / engine | Before → after | |---|---|---| | **Intel Arc B390 iGPU** (laptop, 64 GB unified LPDDR5X, ~115 GB/s) | Ornith-1.5-35B-A3B, EXL3 4 bpw, SGLang XPU + MTP | Decode, 1 user: 43.6 → **53 tok/s** (median)
Decode, 4 users: 84.7 → **103 tok/s**
Prefill 32K: 1,037 → **1,660 tok/s**
Prefill 256K: 297 → **628 tok/s** (2.1×)
KV cache: 264K tokens → **4 × 256K**
Startup: 113 → **43 s**
Registry Lab gates: decode 28.6 → **41.0**, prefill 255 → **667** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Qwen3.8-27B, EXL3 4 bpw, vLLM + custom XPU kernels | Decode: **91.2 tok/s** at 1 user, **365** at 16 (prose, thinking on)
Same card with llama.cpp Q4_K_M: 25.0
Prefill 4K/32K/128K/254K: 1,654/1,434/928/650 → **2,421/2,259/1,415/911**
Agent-session replay: 193 → **147 s** | | **Intel Arc Pro B70** | Same model, SGLang + the same kernels | Decode, 1 user: **82.6 tok/s**, vs vLLM 75.7 on the same card and day | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.8-27B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **96.2 tok/s** prose / **141.1** code, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B EXL3 3 bpw + MTP | **251.7 / 357.9 tok/s**, 1 user | | **RTX 3090** | Flash-Next EXL3, 256K context | MTP: 45.5 → **65.6 tok/s** | | **4× H200 NVL** | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, vLLM + speculative decoding | Crashed under load → **229.1 tok/s** decode, **17,546 tok/s** prefill; all six gates pass | Sources: - [local-ai-registry](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry): - [Ornith B390 recipe](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/tree/main/data/sources/ornith-b390-exl3), with the full hill-climb log in [PR #453](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/local-ai-registry/pull/453) - the RTX 3090 and H200 recipes - [trellis-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/trellis-serve): - `xpu/README.md`, `xpu/docs/PROGRESS.md` and `xpu/docs/SGLANG.md` for B70 - `cuda/README.md` for the RTX 3090 - [qwen-serve](https://github.com/sybil-solutions/qwen-serve) ### Reading the B390 result That run is the one this skill grew out of. Its ceiling calculation said: - **Decode:** 100 tok/s for one user was only reachable with two useful speculative drafts. This model's draft head accepts ~14% at depth 2, so the practical target was ~88–97 tok/s. We reached ~55% of it; the rest is GEMV kernel efficiency. - **Prefill at 256K:** we reached 628 tok/s against a ~670–684 tok/s ceiling. The skill makes the agent compute this up front, so it can tell you early when a target is above the physics. ## How it works ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ measure HW ─▶ │ THEORY.md: bytes/token ÷ bandwidth, FLOPs/token ÷ 50% peak, KV │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ baseline ─▶ profile ─▶ pick lever (ceiling gap × likelihood) ─▶ configs/NEW.json ▲ │ │ queue.sh ctl NEW ctl (serialized, AC-only, │ memory watchdog, ≥6 samples, medians) │ │ PLAN.md + ledger.jsonl ◀── accept only if it beats BOTH neighbouring controls ──┘ │ and regresses nothing by >3% ▼ long-context needle gate ─▶ concurrent full-KV soak ─▶ plateau? ─▶ pinned clean build ─▶ acceptance gates ─▶ publish ``` The skill has three parts: **[`SKILL.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/SKILL.md): the procedure.** - Inventory, ceilings, ground rules, the loop and lever order. - When to stop, how to qualify and publish, and how to report. **[`references/`](skills/inference-optimisation/references): loaded only when needed.** - [`ceilings.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/ceilings.md): how to compute decode, prefill, TTFT, startup and KV maxima, with a worked example. - [`methodology.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/methodology.md): measurement traps. Chunk-counted tokens, mis-sized prompts, acceptance counters, drift, unified-memory accounting. - [`levers.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/levers.md): every lever with measured evidence. It is tagged general vs stack-specific. - [`gotchas.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/gotchas.md): known traps in vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp and ExLlama, and on Intel, NVIDIA, Apple and AMD hardware. - [`publishing.md`](skills/inference-optimisation/references/publishing.md): pinning, clean builds, the six acceptance gates, proving the build matches the best, results cards. **[`scripts/`](skills/inference-optimisation/scripts): a small, engine-agnostic harness.** It is standard-library Python plus bash. - `bench.py` benchmarks any OpenAI-compatible server. It measures: - startup and short-prompt TTFT; - c1 decode (median of N) and cN aggregate decode; - cold prefill at several lengths; - long-context needle retrieval; - peak memory, with a cap watchdog. It flags looping output, failed requests and runs on battery. Token counts come from server usage stats, never from streamed chunks, and everything lands in `ledger.jsonl`. - `ceiling.py` computes the theoretical ceilings from a JSON of measured bandwidth and FLOPs plus component sizes. - `queue.sh` is a serialized, detachable run queue, for interleaving control/candidate/control runs. - `mem.sh` reports a container's real footprint. That includes driver residency on unified-memory GPUs, which cgroups don't see. ## Install Claude Code (user-level): ```bash git clone https://github.com/sybil-solutions/inference-optimisation-skill mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -r inference-optimisation-skill/skills/inference-optimisation ~/.claude/skills/ ``` Then ask, for example: - "hill-climb decode and prefill for the model on :8000 under a 40 GiB cap" - "what's the theoretical max tok/s for this model on this machine?" Other agents: point them at `skills/inference-optimisation/SKILL.md`, or paste [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md) as the task prompt. ## Quick start without an agent ```bash S=skills/inference-optimisation python3 $S/scripts/ceiling.py $S/examples/ceiling-ornith-b390.json # ceilings mkdir -p configs && cp $S/examples/config-existing-server.json configs/base.json # edit base_url/model python3 $S/scripts/bench.py run configs/base.json --long 131072 # one run bash $S/scripts/queue.sh base cand base # interleaved A/B python3 $S/scripts/bench.py show # ledger table ``` ## Principles that carried the most weight - **Ceilings first.** If you don't know the maximum, you can't tell whether 53 tok/s is great or bad, or whether "100 tok/s" is possible. - **Noise is ±5–10%.** Most single-run "wins" are drift. Interleave controls and use medians. - **Measure what matters:** - real tokens, not stream chunks; - real prompt lengths, from the tokenizer; - real memory, including GPU residency on unified memory. - **Speculative decoding is about per-step cost, not acceptance.** - Prune the draft head's vocabulary. - Sweep draft length per concurrency and context. - Keep sampling on the GPU. - **Prove full-context stability** with exact-match needles and a concurrent full-KV soak before calling anything "best". - **Write down failures.** Most of the value in `PLAN.md` is the list of things that did *not* work and why. ## Contributing PRs with new levers, gotchas or results are welcome. Each needs the hardware, model, quantization, engine version, before → after numbers, how they were measured, and a link to raw data. ## License MIT

items.readme:
# Allo Allo is your friendly neighborhood typeface. It’s variable in weight and roundness, with proportions and curves designed to feel warm without being too cute and clear without being too cold. It’s a perfect companion out of the box, and three variable axes and plenty of alternates let you tune its personality to exactly what you need. Allo is optimized for screens and interfaces, with an optical size that adjusts automatically between text and display. And it’s packed with big little details: tabular figures, fractions, punctuation that lifts beside capitals, arrows that appear when you type them, a host of alternates and symbols, as well as a true oblique in every weight. ### [Type specimen at allo.joshpuckett.me →](https://allo.joshpuckett.me)
![Allo: the typeface, and its character set](documentation/readme-row1.png) ![Allo: OpenType features, and interface icons and symbols](documentation/readme-row2.png) ## Download Get `Allo-1.0.3.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/joshpuckett/allo/releases/latest): | Folder | Contents | |---|---| | `fonts/otf` | 18 static fonts, Thin to Black, each with an Oblique | | `fonts/variable` | `AlloVariable.ttf`: all optical sizes, weights and roundnesses | | `fonts/webfonts` | The same fonts as WOFF2, plus `AlloVariableFriendly.woff2` (roundness fixed at 50, about half the size) | The static and variable fonts are separate families, **Allo** and **Allo Variable**, so both can be installed. ## Web From npm: ```sh npm install allo-font ``` ```js import "allo-font"; // the full variable font, and the obliques // import "allo-font/friendly"; // or: roundness fixed at 50, about half the size ``` ```css body { font-family: "Allo", system-ui, sans-serif; } ``` Or host the files yourself, from `fonts/webfonts`: ```css @font-face { font-family: "Allo"; src: url("AlloVariable.woff2") format("woff2"); font-weight: 100 900; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; } body { font-family: "Allo", system-ui, sans-serif; } ``` - **Optical size** follows the font size (`font-optical-sizing: auto`, the CSS default). Set it to `none` to keep the Text design at every size, or pick one with `font-variation-settings: "opsz" 32`. - **Roundness** has no CSS property: use `font-variation-settings: "ROND" 0` (sharp) to `"ROND" 100` (round). Default 50. - **Smaller file:** `AlloVariableFriendly.woff2` has roundness fixed at 50; `"ROND"` has no effect. Its family name is "Allo Variable Friendly". - **Obliques:** the npm CSS includes them. Self-hosting, add an `@font-face` with `font-style: italic` and the matching `font-weight` for each oblique WOFF2 you use (`Allo-Oblique.woff2`, `Allo-BoldOblique.woff2`, …). ## Axes | Axis | Tag | Range | Default | Named values | |---|---|---|---|---| | Optical size | `opsz` | 9–32 | 14 | 9 Small, 14 Text, 32 Display | | Weight | `wght` | 100–900 | 400 | Thin 100 to Black 900 | | Roundness | `ROND` | 0–100 | 50 | 0 Sharp, 50 Friendly, 100 Round | Display (32) is tighter, with stronger optical corrections. Below 14 only the spacing changes. The static fonts are the variable font at opsz 14, ROND 50. ## OpenType features | Feature | Effect | |---|---| | `ss01` Single-story a | ɑ-shaped a | | `ss02` Disambiguation | Serifed I, tailed l, footed 1, slashed zero | | `ss03` Open figures | Open 4, 6 and 9 | | `cv01`–`cv04` | Footed 1, slashed zero, tailed l, serifed I, separately | | `cv05` | Dotted zero | | `tnum` | Tabular figures | | `zero` | Slashed zero | | `frac` | Fractions: 1/2 → ½ | | `sups`, `subs`, `numr`, `dnom` | Superscript, subscript, numerator, denominator | | `case` | Punctuation and symbols raised for capitals | | `liga` | tt, ff, tf, ft with a shared crossbar | | `calt` | `->` → →; brackets, signs, ¿ and ¡ raised beside capitals and figures | Browsers turn ligatures off when letter-spacing is set. For code, use `font-variant-ligatures: no-contextual`. ## Build Python 3.9 or newer: ```sh python3 -m venv .venv .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt .venv/bin/python build.py ``` Writes `fonts/` (variable TTF and WOFF2; 18 static OTFs and WOFF2s, autohinted with AFDKO), `fonts/SHA256SUMS` and `Allo-1.0.3.zip`. Dependencies are pinned and `release.json` fixes the timestamp, so builds are reproducible. ## Sources `sources/Allo.designspace` (designspace 5, UFO) has 48 masters: opsz 9, 14, 20, 32 × wght 100, 400, 580, 900 × ROND 0, 50, 100, plus eight sparse layers at ROND 10 and 30 for heavy joins. The opsz 9 masters are the opsz 14 masters with wider spacing (`release.json` "smallShift"). Corners are rounded in the outlines; the build compiles the sources as they are. Keep points compatible across masters. `sources/static` holds the 18 static fonts' sources: cut from the variable masters at opsz 14, ROND 50, then edited separately. The obliques are separate drawings, not a slant axis. ## Contributing Found a problem, or missing a character? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/joshpuckett/allo/issues); a screenshot and the text you typed help a lot. Pull requests that change the masters or the font files aren't accepted for now. Every change to a letter gets reviewed by eye across all the weights and axes, and that's hard to do well for work that arrives from outside. If you have a larger idea, such as a new script, open an issue first so we can talk about it. You're free to modify Allo and ship your own version under the [license](OFL.txt). ## License [SIL Open Font License 1.1](OFL.txt): free to use, modify and redistribute, including commercially. The fonts can't be sold by themselves. ## Credit Allo began from [Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) 4.2, which provided an incredible base to work from. Every one of Allo's glyphs has been redrawn, with extensive work on spacing, kerning, features and axes, all tuned for the friendly character that makes Allo its own. I owe a huge debt of gratitude to my friend [Rasmus Andersson](https://rsms.me) for creating Inter and releasing it under an open license; without it, Allo would not exist. Allo also pays homage to Honk Sans by [Seb McLauchlan](https://www.sebmclauchlan.com) and aims to bring some of that same warmth and fun to everyone.

Steer your ideas in realtime, space pilot style!

Watch on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfyQPhFtW-z/) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WmNLWUmcnY). You can try the simulator at [https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/) with the option to go live with your API keys for Cerebras and Gemini. Keys stay in your browser local storage. Do it at your own risk.

## Conjecture

> In the near future, LLM and Decision Models will reach 60 FPS interactivity.

When that happens, what new interaction paradigms will unlock? This project demonstrates plausible and desirable interactions for that future.

1. **Focus monitor**: can we visualize what LLM is paying attention to, and use that to guide human's focus towards what's important?

   ![focus monitor](./extra/clips/focus-monitor.gif)

2. **Attention lock**: can we force LLM to pay more attention to specific phrases so as to bias its future behavior?

   ![attention lock](./extra/clips/attention-lock.gif)

3. **Future Vector Steering**: can we decompose the task into eigenvectors, independently tune each, and re-compose them to influence the incoming text?

   ![future steering](./extra/clips/future-steering.gif)

4. **Realtime re-generation**: when text generation is cheap and fast, can we explore alternative futures by scrubbing?

   ![realtime regeneration](./extra/clips/realtime-regeneration.gif)

## Design process

I used Claude Code for most of the implementation but stayed hands-on for the UI/UX. I iterate using interactive style swatch, a technique where I prompt AI to give me diverse options of designs, I provide feedback, and it iterates. You can see the design artifacts in the [extra page](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/extra/style-1.html).

To achieve the realtime experience, I have to use agreesive speculative generation and manage cache invalidation based on user interactions. For example, when the main knob moves backward, I have to empty future texts and cancel ongoing requests. There are many considerations like this throughout the system and that took a lot of human judgement - claude didn't one shot them.

## Theory

I'm currently focusing on systems that help human shape ideas in realtime. This project is a small step towards my [upcoming thesis](https://code.chuanqisun.com/master-thesis/) at the MIT Media Lab, where I investigate how semantic and symoblic systems can be coupled to enhance human creativity, agency, and joy of craft.

items.readme:
# Google One 工具包（MuMu 模拟器 + Frida）

**`g1.30tb`已在大部分区域下架，可以先搞搞3个月打折的Ultra 5X**

通过 Frida 注入模拟器里的 Google One 进程，调用 Play BillingClient：
**扫描账号可用的全部订阅 offer（免费/付费）**，以及**拉起任意 SKU 的 Play 收银台**（只弹出，不自动订阅）。

---

## 文件清单

| 文件 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `ultra0_core.py` | 自包含核心（adb/frida-server/计费模块/注入模板，从原 ultra0.py 抽取） |
| `extract_core.py` | 生成器：从原版 ultra0.py 重新抽取 ultra0_core.py（仅维护时用） |
| `one_common.py` | 公共环境准备（选设备/root/frida-server/计费模块/Play 商店保活），所有脚本共用 |
| `launch_checkout.py` + `launch_checkout.js` | **拉起任意 SKU 收银台**（主力脚本） |
| `scan_all.py` | 全量扫描 70 个候选 SKU 的所有 offer（免费+付费+token），零风险 |
| `query_sku.py` | 只查指定几个 SKU，零风险 |
| `probe_env.py` | 环境诊断（frida 版本 / Java 桥 / Play 商店状态），出问题先跑它 |
| `scan_everything.py` + `scan_offers.js` | 穷举账号全部 SKU，输出带定价阶段的原始 JSON 并渲染清单 |
| `render_multi.py` | 合并多地区 JSON，生成 `SKU-清单.md` |
| `scan_result_*.json` | 各地区扫描原始数据（已脱敏：serial 已掩码、token 已置空） |
| `SKU-清单.md` | 多地区金额对照 + 人民币比价清单 |

> 整个文件夹**自包含、无外部依赖**：把 `google-one-tools` 拷到任何机器（装有
> Python3.9+ 和 frida 16.x）都能直接跑，不需要原版仓库里的脚本。

## 环境要求（缺一不可）

1. **本机 frida 必须 16.x**（推荐 16.7.19）：
   ```powershell
   py -m pip install frida==16.7.19
   ```
   > ⚠️ frida 17.x 在 MuMu（Android 12 / x86_64）上 Java 桥损坏（`Java is not defined`），
   > 所有功能静默失效。设备上的 frida-server 也必须同版本（脚本会自动下载匹配版）。
2. **自包含核心**：所有对原版 `ultra0.py` 的依赖已抽取进 `ultra0_core.py`，
   本文件夹可整体拷贝到别处使用；要更新抽取范围，改 `extract_core.py` 后重跑 `py extract_core.py`。
3. 模拟器已 root、已登录 Google 账号、装有 Google One 和 Play 商店。
4. 用 `py` 而不是 `python`（本机的 `python` 是商店占位符，跑不了）。

## 快速上手

```powershell
cd C:\path\to\google-one-tools

# 0. 环境自检（第一次先跑这个）
py probe_env.py

# 1. 扫描当前账号的全部 offer（免费+付费，不下单）
py scan_all.py                       # 自动选第一台模拟器
py scan_all.py 127.0.0.1:16384       # 多开时指定实例

# 2. 只查某几个 SKU
py query_sku.py g1.30tb g1.20tb

# 3. 拉起收银台（弹出后人工确认，脚本不点订阅）
py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.20tb                    # 自动选设备
py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.30tb 127.0.0.1:16384    # 指定实例
```

## SKU 对照表

| 档位 | SKU | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 30 GB / 100GB / 200GB | `g1.30gb` / `g1.100gb` / `g1.200gb` | 基础存储 |
| 2TB / 5TB / 10TB / 20TB / 30TB | `g1.2tb` / `g1.5tb` / `g1.10tb` / `g1.20tb` / `g1.30tb` | 基础存储 |
| 年付版 | 上面任一 + `.annual`（如 `g1.2tb.annual`） | 部分档无年付 |
| AI Plus (400GB) | `g1.play.helium` | 常有 12/6/3/1 月免费试用 |
| AI Pro (5TB) | `g1.2tb.ai.subs_variant` | 常有 12+6+6+6 月免费试用 |
| Ultra 20TB | `g1.play.20tb` | 试用看账号资格 |
| Ultra AI Pro (30TB) | `g1.play.ai.pro` / `g1.30tb` | 多数号无试用 |
| 2TB 首三月折扣 | `g1.2tb.3months_ip_85p.acq` | introprice，非免费 |

> 免费试用档基本只挂在**带 `play` 前缀**或 **`subs_variant`** 的 SKU 上；
> 带 `.eft` 后缀的是试用专用 SKU。以 `scan_all.py` 的实际返回为准。

## 多模拟器实例

- `pick_device` 默认选 adb 列表第一台。**多开时必须指定**：位置参数或环境变量 `SERIAL`：
  ```powershell
  py launch_checkout.py --sku g1.20tb 127.0.0.1:16384
  $env:SERIAL="127.0.0.1:16384"; py scan_all.py
  ```
  （`16384` 只是 MuMu 12 的默认 ADB 端口；多开实例的实际端口以 `adb devices` 为准。）
- frida 连接按 serial 精确匹配，不会串台。

## VPN 共存（本工具包刻意支持）

- **不调用** `ultra0.ensure_network()`：不清设备代理、不杀 Clash/v2rayNG。
- 注入走 adb 通道（127.0.0.1:xxxxx），与模拟器内 VPN 互不影响。
- 建议 VPN 用**分应用模式**，排除这三个包让结算直连：
  `com.android.vending`、`com.google.android.gms`、`com.google.android.apps.subscriptions.red`
  （或 TUN 模式把 DNS 从 fake-ip 改 redir-host，否则 Play 结算可能连不上。）

## 故障排查（按命中频率排序）

| 症状 | 原因 | 解法 |
|---|---|---|
| 收银台不弹出、Play 商店像是「死了」；logcat 有 `InAppBillingService ... crashed service` / `Monetization gRPC call timeout` / `:recovery_mode failed to attach` | **VPN（如 Surfshark）劫持了 Play 的网络**，结算服务崩溃重启 | ① Surfshark → 设置 → VPN 设置 → 分应用代理(Split tunneling) → 排除 `Google Play 商店`、`Google Play 服务`、`Google One`；② 或跑收银台前先断开 VPN |
| 未收到 `launched` 事件 | Play 商店没在跑（脚本会自动拉，但可能拉不起来） | 跑 `py probe_env.py` 看 vending 状态 |
| Play 商店反复 `failed to attach` / `start timeout` | Play 商店假死（连拉多次收银台后常见） | **重启模拟器**：`adb -s <serial> reboot`，10 秒开机不亏 |
| 收银台弹出瞬间 Play 商店崩（ScionFrontendAp SIGABRT） | MuMu 镜像上 Play 商店老版本 bug | 模拟器里升级 Play 商店，或清其数据 |
| Java 桥 `hasJava:false` | 本机或设备 frida 是 17.x | `py -m pip install frida==16.7.19`，删设备 `/data/local/tmp/frida-server` 重跑 |
| 重启模拟器后脚本报「没有 root」 | adb root 后 adbd 瞬断 | 本工具包的 `ensure_root_retry` 已自动重试；旧脚本需手动 `adb -s <serial> root` |
| 查询空 offer | frida 坏了（Java 桥死）或 SKU 在该账号地区不存在 | 先 `probe_env.py`；再看 SKU 是否在该地区上架 |

## 重要注意

- `launchBillingFlow` 返回 code=0 **即可能消耗该账号的试用资格**，即使你最后没点订阅——别对同一个号反复拉免费档。
- 收银台弹出不点订阅不会扣费；点了订阅按显示价格扣费。
- 免费试用结束会自动续费，记得提前取消。
